description: This file defines the Layout class and associated functions for manipulating tensor layouts, including coalescing, filtering, composition, inversion, and hierarchical operations, specifically for use within the PyTorch distributed module. It handles layout transformations based on lexicographic ordering and includes utility functions for shape and stride manipulations.

classes.name: Layout
classes.description: Represents a tensor layout with shape and stride, providing methods for mapping coordinates, slicing, size calculations, and string representations.

methods.name: make_layout
methods.description: Constructs a Layout object from one or more Layouts or shape/stride tuples.

methods.name: size
methods.description: Returns the total number of elements in the layout's domain.

methods.name: cosize
methods.description: Returns the size of the layout's codomain.

methods.name: coalesce
methods.description: Flattens and merges layout modes to simplify the layout while preserving the index mapping.

methods.name: filter
methods.description: Removes stride-0 modes and merges adjacent modes with compatible shape and stride.

methods.name: composition
methods.description: Composes two layouts, combining their shape and stride information.

methods.name: complement
methods.description: Computes the complement of a layout up to a maximum index.

methods.name: right_inverse
methods.description: Computes the right inverse of a layout.

methods.name: left_inverse
methods.description: Computes the left inverse of a layout.

methods.name: logical_divide
methods.description: Hierarchically divides one layout by another.

methods.name: hier_unzip
methods.description: Unzips hierarchical layout operations into separate modes.

methods.name: zipped_divide
methods.description: Hierarchically divides layouts and gathers modes.

methods.name: zipped_product
methods.description: Hierarchically multiplies layouts and gathers modes.

methods.name: slice_and_offset
methods.description: Creates a sublayout from a coordinate and computes its offset.
